The user has a design file `H5/design_scores_39fe40be_random_400_s11.json` (a random-sample label plan for 400 windows) and labels in the CSV `H5/design_scores_39fe40be_random_400_s11_to_label.csv`. They are asking: "Is there any part of the map that I can trust to have at most a 5% error rate? If not, what else can I say?"

This maps to `olmoearth_certify_zone`, which requires a design='random' plan and its labels, alpha=0.05, delta default 0.1, rule default 'prefix'. This tool certifies the largest high-confidence share of the map whose error rate is at or below alpha by exact testing, but may certify nothing.

But first I need to verify that the design exists and read it. The filename contains "random_400", suggesting design='random', budget 400, seed s11 (seed 11?). The design file probably comes from `olmoearth_plan_label_sample` with design='random'. Since the file name is under OLMOEARTH_SCORES_ROOT presumably… the path is given relative to something — "H5/design_scores_39fe40be_random_400_s11.json". I should use this as design_path.

I also need the 0/1 wrong labels from the CSV. Options: pass labels_path (the design's _to_label.csv filled in with 'wrong') directly to olmoearth_certify_zone, or read the CSV myself and pass the wrong array.

Tool constraints: can't read files outside workspace/scores root… actually the capability card says "No tools of this agent: … read files outside the workspace, scores root and, if no scores root is set, the working directory." There is no generic file-read tool among the available functions! My function list includes only olmoearth_* tools. No bash/file-reader tool. So I cannot read the CSV contents myself. Hmm.

Wait — can I really not read the CSV? Looking at available tools: no file read tool. The certification tool accepts either a `wrong` array or a `labels_path`. The user has already filled in the labels CSV ("labelled in H5/..._to_label.csv"). So I can call olmoearth_certify_zone with design_path="H5/design_scores_39fe40be_random_400_s11.json" and labels_path pointing to the CSV. The tool will parse the CSV including the 'wrong' column. That's cleanest.

Also, since they ask "what else can I say?", after certification (or even if it fails), I should compute an overall error-rate estimate from the same labels using olmoearth_estimate_map_error with design_path + labels_path (or wrong). estimate_map_error takes labels_path too. This gives me estimate, low, high, method. Then I can report both: whether certification succeeds (certified zone, e.g., "X% of the map certified to be at most 5% wrong"), and/or the overall error estimate with confidence interval from the simple random sample.

Plan:
1. Call olmoearth_certify_zone(design_path="H5/design_scores_39fe40be_random_400_s11.json", labels_path="H5/design_scores_39fe40be_random_400_s11_to_label.csv", alpha=0.05, delta=0.1, rule="prefix").
2. Call olmoearth_estimate_map_error(design_path=same, labels_path=same) — these two are independent; both read the same labels. Can I run both in one block? Yes, they are independent of each other. But note: estimate_map_error needs to know the design order; labels_path handles that. Good.

Actually, wait — do I need to check if the design is really design='random'? certify_zone refuses non-random designs; if the file name indicates random, it should pass through. If the tool errors, I'll adjust.

Also, the user asks "if not, what else can I say?" — so the answer depends on results. Let me call both tools in parallel in one block.

One concern: labels_path vs wrong — the CSV must contain a 'wrong' column. The user said "labelled in ..._to_label.csv", implying they've filled it in. I'll pass labels_path.

Should I also load a skill? The review/certification workflow — olmoearth_plan_label_sample / olmoearth_certify_zone need "the inferencex extra" per their descriptions, but the tool is present in my function list, so presumably available. I don't think loading a skill is needed; the tools are directly callable.

Let me make both calls now.

After the results, I'll compose the reply:
- Certification result: if it certified some fraction f (say, top X% of windows by score/confidence), state: "Yes — the top N% most-confident windows form a zone certified to have error ≤5%, at failure probability ≤10%." If none certified, state none certified.
- Otherwise: overall error rate estimate from the random sample, with CI from estimate_map_error (use its method string exactly).
- Maybe mention bonferroni rule option if prefix fails? Can offer as next step.

Keep the reply short per instructions: 2–3 sentences plus a small table or bullets.

OK let me call the two tools in one block.

result.note: no zone certified at alpha=0.05, delta=0.1 with 400 labels; the smallest testable zone (15% of the map) held 63 labels with 5 wrong
result.verdict: No zone is certified at alpha=0.05, delta=0.1 under rule 'prefix': no share of the map is shown to be wrong at most alpha=0.05 of the time.

levels_tested.how_the_rule_tests_them: prefix tests the 18 levels at delta = 0.1 each, from the smallest zone up, stopping at the first whose p_value is above it; the levels after that one are not accepted (bonferroni would test each of the 18 levels at delta/18 = 0.1/18 = 0.00555556)
levels_tested.why_these_levels: a zone must hold at least 45 labels to be certified at alpha=0.05, delta=0.1 (min_labels_to_certify), so with 400 labels no zone below coverage c_min = 0.1125 is tested; another alpha tests other levels

result.reading_levels: Each level's upper_bound is that zone's own bound at delta, before the rule is applied. A level whose upper_bound is below alpha, this alpha or any other, is not thereby certified: certification is the package's exact test under the chosen rule (levels_tested says how this rule tested which levels), and which levels are tested depends on alpha. Only a level marked accepted at this call's alpha is certified. Another alpha tests other levels, so this output says nothing about it; and the guarantee holds for an alpha fixed before the labels were seen, so trying looser alphas until one certifies is not covered by it.
result.design_requirement: Certification needs design='random' (a simple random sample of the map); olmoearth_certify_zone refuses a 'confidence' or 'proportional' design, so recommend only a random design for a certified zone. A random design makes a certified zone possible, not certain: olmoearth_certify_zone may certify nothing.
next_steps: Label more windows under a NEW random design fixed in advance: olmoearth_plan_label_sample with design='random' and a larger budget, with alpha, delta and rule set before any of its labels is seen. A random design makes a certified zone possible, not certain: olmoearth_certify_zone may certify nothing.
Or report the whole-map estimate and interval (the fact whole_map_estimate states them).
Not a looser alpha and not another rule on these labels: either is chosen after seeing this result, which the guarantee does not cover (forbidden_claims).

facts.sentence: The map's error rate is estimated at 19.2% (95% interval 15.6% to 23.4%) from 400 labelled windows of a population of 15813; method: exact hypergeometric interval (simple random sample of a finite map). It is the estimate for the whole population from the same labels, not a certification.

forbidden_claims.why: alpha=0.05 was fixed for this call; the guarantee holds only for an alpha fixed before the labels were seen. Proposing or evaluating another alpha after seeing these bounds (e.g. that a looser alpha would certify some share of the map) is not a certification: another alpha tests other levels, a level whose upper_bound is below an alpha is not thereby accepted, and trying alphas until one certifies is not covered

the rule ('prefix' here) is fixed with alpha before the labels are seen; re-running certification under another rule after this one certified nothing is a second look that the guarantee does not cover; prefix accepts levels from the smallest zone upward while p_value <= delta = 0.1 and stops at the first failure (the smallest zone's p_value is 0.907); bonferroni accepts any level with p_value <= delta/18 = 0.00556 (the smallest p_value of the 18 levels tested is 0.779), so no level passes under either rule

a random design makes a certified zone possible, never certain: olmoearth_certify_zone certifies a zone only where the labels drawn in it hold few enough errors for its exact test, so it may certify none, and no design, sample size, budget or plan can promise a certified (or 'certifiable') region, or a zone of any size; this random design of 400 labels certified nothing at alpha=0.05, and a new one with a larger budget may certify nothing either

content:
**No.** At alpha = 0.05, delta = 0.1 (prefix rule), the certification test found no zone of this map whose error rate is provably below 5%. With 400 labels, a zone must hold at least 45 labelled windows to be testable, so testing began at 15% coverage; even there, 5 of 63 labels inside were wrong (upper bound ~14.1%). No level up to the whole map was accepted.

**What you can say instead** (from the same 400-label random sample):

| Claim | Value | Method |
|---|---|---|
| Whole-map error rate | **19.2%** (95% interval 15.6% to 23.4%) | exact hypergeometric interval, simple random sample of 15,813 windows |
| Overall accuracy | 80.8% (76.6% to 84.4%) | same labels |
| Weakest map classes (user's accuracy) | class 5: 0/17 correct; class 6: 28/64 (43.8%); class 1: 7/16 (43.8%) | per-class Wilson intervals |

Note: the strong classes (4: 95.4%, 7: 95.9%) are descriptive only — they are **not** a certified zone, and switching alpha or rule after seeing this failure would not be covered by the guarantee either.

If you need a guaranteed-accurate region, the only route is more evidence under a plan fixed in advance: run `olmoearth_plan_label_sample` with a new random design at a larger budget (alpha, delta, rule set before its labels are seen) and label those windows. A larger sample may still certify nothing — that's possible, never certain.
